est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données
stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage).

Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe.

Ce que vous ferez

Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.
Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données.
Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données.
Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance.
Développer des indicateurs de gouvernance, des KPI de santé des données et des rapports destinés à la haute direction.
Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.
Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

Exigences de base

Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.
Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.
Expérience en gestion de la qualité des données, traçabilité des données, intendance des données et contrôles de gouvernance.
Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes de conformité, de gestion des risques, de protection de la vie privée, d’audit ou de réglementation.
Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.
Expérience dans l’élaboration de politiques, de normes, de KPI et de cadres de reddition de comptes en matière de gouvernance.

Compétences et expérience privilégiées

Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés tels que les soins de santé, les produits pharmaceutiques, les services financiers ou l’assurance.
Connaissance de plateformes de gouvernance des données telles que Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview ou des outils similaires.
Expérience avec les principes DAMA-DMBOK et les cadres de gestion des données d’entreprise.
Connaissance des règlements en matière de protection des données, des mécanismes de gouvernance et des cadres de gestion des risques.
Expérience à diriger des initiatives de transformation des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Excellentes compétences en communication auprès des dirigeants et en gestion du changement organisationnel.
Certifications pertinentes en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, protection de la vie privée ou technologies infonuagiques.

Déplacements, environnement de travail et exigences physiques

Capacité à voyager jusqu’à 20 % du temps, selon les besoins de l’entreprise.
Modalités de travail hybrides ou à distance pouvant être offertes selon les besoins de l’entreprise et la situation géographique.
Capacité à participer à des réunions virtuelles et en personne et à travailler efficacement dans un environnement soutenu par la technologie.

About The Role

McKesson is seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Data Governance to lead enterprise-wide data governance programs that improve data quality, regulatory compliance, business trust, and operational excellence. This leader will define and execute governance strategies across data governance, metadata management, data cataloging, data quality, master data management, and data lineage capabilities.

The Director will partner with business, technology, risk, compliance, and data leaders to establish governance frameworks, standards, policies, and controls that support data-driven decision making and regulatory requirements. This role requires a strong combination of leadership, stakeholder engagement, data management expertise, and the ability to influence outcomes across a complex enterprise environment.

What You'll Do

Lead enterprise data governance strategy, operating model, policies, standards, and controls.
Drive adoption and optimization of data governance and data catalog platforms.
Establish and oversee data quality, metadata management, master data, and data lineage programs.
Partner with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, Security, and Audit teams to ensure regulatory compliance and governance readiness.
Develop governance metrics, data health KPIs, and executive reporting for senior leadership.
Engage business stakeholders to define data ownership, stewardship, accountability, and governance priorities.
Lead cross-functional teams delivering large-scale governance and data management initiatives.
Build and develop high-performing teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Basic Requirements

12+ years of professional experience in data governance, data management, data architecture, analytics, compliance, or related disciplines, including 4+ years of people leadership experience.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Experience leading enterprise-scale data governance programs and operating models.
Experience implementing or managing data catalog, metadata management, or governance platforms.
Experience with data quality management, data lineage, data stewardship, and governance controls.
Experience partnering with compliance, risk, privacy, audit, or regulatory organizations.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders.
Experience defining governance policies, standards, KPIs, and reporting frameworks.

Preferred Skills/Experience

Master's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Business, Data Analytics, or a related field.
Experience supporting regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceutical, financial services, or insurance.
Knowledge of data governance platforms such as Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview, or similar tools.
Experience with DAMA-DMBOK principles and enterprise data management frameworks.
Knowledge of data privacy regulations, governance controls, and risk management frameworks.
Experience leading enterprise-wide data transformation initiatives.
Strong executive communication and organizational change management capabilities.
Relevant certifications related to data governance, data management, privacy, or cloud technologies.

Ability to travel up to 20% as business needs require.
Hybrid or remote work arrangements may be available based on business and geographic requirements.
Ability to participate in virtual and in-person meetings and work effectively in a technology-enabled environment.

jobs.description:
Help enterprises put AI agents to work in customer experience.

Most enterprise support teams have spent years building on platforms they rely on every day. Those platforms hold their tickets, workflows, knowledge and customer history. What's missing is AI that can actually do the work: resolve issues, take action across systems and hold up at enterprise scale.
That's what Botpress does. We're the enterprise-grade AI agent platform for customer experience, backed by a $25 million Series B. Over 1 million AI agents run in production on Botpress, and more than 4,000 customers use the platform, including American Express and GE. We pioneered tool calling for AI agents and were the first to bring a commercial retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offering to market.
We work alongside the systems our customers already use, integrating and partnering with them to make them work better.
At Botpress, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective and talents. We work fully in-office in Montreal. If you want to help build what comes next, we'd like to meet you.

About the Role

We're hiring a Director of Sales to lead our team of three account executives through a pivot into a more consultative, sales-led motion with mid-market and enterprise companies. You'll report to our CRO and work closely together to find product-market fit in a new category, then build the team to scale it. This is a hands-on role: you'll be in deals alongside your AEs at critical moments, and you'll grow the team with us, with a seat in hiring from day one. The role is based in our Montreal office.
Responsibilities

Lead and develop the sales team.
Coach and lead our account executives as a hands-on leader, and grow the team with us. Set clear expectations and build a culture of curiosity, accountability and consistent execution
Own the forecast and pipeline.
Run a weekly operating rhythm with rigorous forecasting, pipeline reviews and deal inspection in HubSpot. Translate our revenue goals into account priorities, pipeline targets and coverage, and drive the team to hit them
Guide complex deals from discovery to signature.
Coach sellers through multi-stakeholder buying committees using MEDDPICC or a similar framework, and engage directly at critical moments. Bring in Solutions Engineering, security, legal and leadership for business cases, technical validation, pricing and negotiation
Turn pilots into contracts.
Make sure each pilot has a clear scope, agreed success measures, a defined spend cap and terms that convert it to an annual contract. Help the team navigate budget timing, procurement and security reviews, and lead deal reviews that surface risk early and turn it into clear next steps
Help define product-market fit.
Test what resonates with mid-market and enterprise buyers, read the signals in our pipeline, and tell us plainly what's working and what isn't. Bring market signals and customer feedback to Product and leadership to shape where Botpress goes next
Partner with outbound and Marketing.
Work with our outbound team and Marketing on account segmentation, targeting, messaging and account-based plays. Give them regular, specific feedback on what converts so pipeline quality improves every month
Build a repeatable go-to-market motion.
Turn what works into stages, playbooks, enablement and metrics the team can run without you in the room. Once product-market fit is established, build the hiring model and capacity plan: headcount, ramp and pipeline coverage
Lead an AI-native sales team.
Embed AI into how the team researches accounts, develops outreach, prepares for calls, plans deals and forecasts. Model it yourself, share what works, and help sellers spend more time on judgment, strategy and customer relationships

Requirements

8+ years in B2B SaaS sales, including 3+ years leading account executives in mid-market or enterprise
A track record closing complex, committee-driven deals using MEDDIC, MEDDPICC or a similar framework
Experience running pilots or proofs of value that converted to paid contracts
Experience leading sellers alongside solutions engineers, and working with outbound and ABM programs
Technical fluency: comfortable in conversations about APIs, integrations, data and security
Experience building or rebuilding a sales motion at an early-stage or scaling company, and comfortable when the playbook is still being written
Bonus: experience selling AI or customer support technology, or leading a team through a change in market or motion; French

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is a senior leadership position within UBC Facilities. The Director provides strategic leadership for Facilities customer service function, customer service plan, business project management, business analysis, informatics, enterprise maintenance management system (EMMS), facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This role develops strategic objectives, implements and monitors procedures and policies that enable Facilities to meet or exceed agreed customer service standards across the entire campus. In addition, this division provides all business units within Facilities the necessary business support both by providing the necessary analytics and analysis to ensure continuous improvements continue across the department. The Director is responsible for the development and sustainment of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan.

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is the Facilities representative for customer engagement, business projects and initiatives, space inventory data, building and infrastructure records drawings and information, analytics, reporting, technology and continuous improvement initiatives. They partner with Information Technology (IT) and Safety and Risk Services (SRS) - Emergency Management, Project Management Office (PMO), Integrated Service Centre (ISC), Communications & Engagement for strategic alignment and resource allocation.

The Director leads a workforce of approximately 35 staff in professional and unionized positions. Prepares strategic and business plans and supports an annual Facilities budget of approximately $150M.

Organizational Status

This position reports directly to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, and serves as a member of the Facilities Leadership team. Works closely with other Directors, Senior Managers, and Managers as well as other department‘s leadership teams. This position is the senior leader within Facilities responsible for implementing business transformational initiatives with the support of other divisions, monitoring operational progress through the analysis and reporting of information to guide evidence-based decision-making.

Work Performed

Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Leadership team through the Customer Services and Informatics division to execute a full range of department-wide services to meet targets and objectives of the Strategic Plan. This includes supporting and developing business plans; ensuring consistent and effective implementation; enhancing integration; standardizing services and business practices; maximizing efficiencies and cost savings.
Responsible for business transformational projects through assessment, analysis, design and implementation; champions the implementation of change management initiatives, process and execution.
Leads the development of a Monitoring Framework with key performance indicators for each unit within the department and develops remedial and continuous improvement plans in relation to results. This framework includes leading and lagging indicators and an effective client satisfaction monitoring and reporting system to evaluate the services provided by the entire Facilities group.
Leads the facilities information and inventory systems function, including university space inventory data, building and infrastructure record drawings, key plans, emergency response plans, and maintenance manuals.
Provides direction and implements change management methodologies to effectively lead and optimize key projects across Facilities.
Mentors and coaches change management in relation to the implementation of business initiatives.
Liaises with academic, administrative and ancillary customers, engineers, architects and external clients to ensure that the facilities needs of the university are being met.
Supports and provides direction to the Senior Facilities Manager in providing strategic leadership to the Facilities Managers working in the geographic zone model. Through the Senior Facilities Manager, oversees the delivery of equal, consistent and effectively prioritized service delivery within the campus zones.
Provides strategic leadership on sustainment of Facilities and University information systems in support of enterprise maintenance management, asset management, stores inventory, space inventory, records drawings, records management, and project management.
Provides strategic leadership and/or oversees development of innovative business solutions and services that integrate data and reporting capabilities to augment decision-making.
Oversees work of various teams performing quality testing of data and information and reconciling across sources, presenting facts and evidence in dashboards to assist in effective evidence-based decision making.
Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Service Centre who are responsible for handling inbound and outbound calls regarding buildings and grounds.
Responsible for administrative/clerical support services for the Facilities group.
Provides direction in the completion of regulatory and skills development training for all staff within Facilities which includes developing plans, implementing and evaluating, department-wide strategies.
Leads and directs the development of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan, including emergency preparedness exercises for the department in collaboration with SRS, Emergency Management.
Works with SRS and implements consistent health, safety and environmental initiatives, which, includes safety committee, accident investigations, safety training and safety recommendations within the Customer Services and Informatics division.
Responsible for human resource practices including recruitment, orientation, training, performance evaluation, discipline, labor relations and dismissal within the Customer Services and Informatics division in collaboration with Human Resources.
Performs other related duties, including but not limited to:
Representing Facilities on various university committees. Develops working relationships and partnerships with key stakeholders across UBC.
Acting on behalf of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

Facilities plays a key role in enabling the University to achieve its goal of becoming one of the world‘s leading universities. The Director Customer Services and Informatics position is critical to the success of Facilities and the complex services that it provides. The Director must apply judgment, tact and discretion due to the broad and extensive implications for success in the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, information system management, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. The Director plays an important part in the formulation, alignment and implementation of the strategic initiatives and managing the outcomes and impacts on operations and the services they provide.

Failure to ensure alignment and direction for Facilities in this role will negatively impact on the reputation of the University. The consequence of poor decisions have human resources, legal and representational consequences and in addition to costs. Failure to effectively direct major projects that transform business operations through change or to ensure accurate asset information for facilities planning, major capital decisions, or maintenance, construction and renovation activities will lead to the loss of millions of dollars in investment, inefficiencies or unrealized efficiency benefits, and potential safety issues.

Supervision Given

The Director is directly responsible for supervising work of 6 professional staff in manager and senior manager roles, with a diverse portfolio of supporting units including the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This position will also act as the Associate Vice-President, Facilities from time to time.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, and our consumer product launches in January. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast and controls across our entities in Canada and China. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
Investor reporting: the financial model and board and investor updates
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and the numbers hold up to any scrutiny.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

As we scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
Investor reporting: the financial model and board and investor updates
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and the numbers hold up to any scrutiny.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them

You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

As we scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

A sensor for your parents, on us

Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure

THE OPPORTUNITY

We have a dynamic opportunity for a Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer (CMSO) to join the Executive Leadership Team at Alberta Municipalities in Edmonton, Alberta. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the CMSO is the enterprise integrator for strategy, corporate planning and governance, strategic project management, growth and innovation, and marketing and communications. This is a great role for a leader that thrives in a fast paced and complex senior leadership role, managing multiple competing priorities, in an agile decision-making hub for member priorities. The corporate governance oversight and accountabilities associated with the role are significant and deep experience with Board governance is necessary for success.

The CMSO leads five direct reports: four Senior Directors, responsible for Corporate Planning and Governance, Project Management, Growth and Innovation, and Marketing and Communications, and a Project Coordinator/Executive Assistant. Working in a multifaceted environment, the CMSO makes sense of complex and emerging issues, frames them for decisions by the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team, Boards and Committees, and leads the plans, programs and projects that turn strategy into measurable results for members.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a senior strategic leader who thrives in complexity, is a strong and effective communicator and has a deep background in corporate governance. The CMSO will turn ambiguous and competing information into clear strategy and plain language so that Boards, elected officials and executives can act on and set priorities across the organization aligning resources where they create the most value. They bring strong business and corporate service acumen along with a delivery focused mindset that can balance delegating vs perfection, and the judgement and diplomacy to advise on sensitive matters. They will also have the experience and background to effectively work with internal and external partners and stakeholders as well as elected officials and various levels of government.

As a true partner and a leader of people, the successful candidate brings strong emotional intelligence, integrity, a corporate services mindset, earns trust, and builds alignment through influence. They adjudicate objectively between competing views, support productive debate, contribute to dialogue constructively, lean into difficult conversations and step in directly when the team is stretched. They coach senior leaders, draw on the experience of the team, model the organization’s values, and strengthen a collaborative, accountable and high-performing culture, staying calm and fact based in a fast-moving, political environment. They also need to be passionate about the work of municipalities and the people they lead.

THE ORGANIZATION

Founded in 1905, Alberta Municipalities (ABmunis) is the province’s largest municipal association. It represents 264 of Alberta’s 334 municipalities, from small summer villages to major cities and specialized municipalities, which together are home to more than 85% of Albertans. It advocates on shared municipal issues and helps members build resilient communities. It also pools its members’ purchasing power to secure better pricing on employee benefits, insurance, energy and other services, with the proceeds helping fund its advocacy work. Its business services and its advocacy reinforce each other, and it works through partnerships to build common solutions with its members.

Governance

Alberta Municipalities is led by a Board of Directors elected by member municipalities during each annual convention. The Board is comprised of representatives from Alberta’s cities, towns, villages, summer villages, and specialized municipalities.

Additional information about Alberta Municipalities and key resources relevant to this opportunity are available below:
Alberta Municipalities website
2026 Advocacy Priorities
ABmunis Media Releases
ABmunis 2025 year in review

RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership and Issues Management

Lead how the organization identifies, assesses and responds to complex and emerging issues, risks and opportunities, drawing on governance, member, advocacy, business, financial, operational, technology and reputational perspectives.
Distill ambiguous issues into clear problem statements, strategic choices and recommendations, and advise the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team and the Boards on significant and sensitive matters.
Develop frameworks, strategies and roadmaps with clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success, and lead cross functional work on issues that span departments, entities or governance bodies.
Help develop advocacy strategies that advance member priorities with different levels of government and stakeholder groups, building alignment among people with different mandates and perspectives.

Corporate Planning and Governance

Provide executive leadership for governance across multiple (5) Boards, (9) committees and legal entities, respecting their distinct mandates and regulatory requirements, including agenda planning, decision support, appointments and the implementation of Board direction, and ensure Board and committee meetings are well run, with timely, high-quality materials.
Lead strategic planning and evaluation with the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team and the Boards, turning Board direction into organizational priorities, initiatives and performance measures.
Direct environmental scanning of political, economic, social, regulatory, member, market and technology trends, and advance governance effectiveness and Board development.
Oversee the corporate policy framework so policies are developed, reviewed, approved, communicated and applied consistently, in line with legislation and strategy, and oversee Board election processes, including Returning Officer responsibilities.

Strategy Execution and Program/Project Management

Lead the Project Management Office, setting the approach to prioritization, intake, governance, resourcing, risk and reporting, and the level of involvement based on an initiative’s complexity, risk and impact.
Oversee a portfolio of strategic and operational initiatives, including digital transformation (enterprise systems, data, CRM, automation), organizational and process transformation, governance initiatives, business growth, member programs, advocacy and public policy campaigns, and complex regulatory and compliance implementations.
Ensure major initiatives have clear objectives, scope, accountabilities, resources, timelines, risks and success measures before implementation, resolve competing priorities and capacity constraints with sponsors, and keep senior leaders and Boards informed of progress, risks and results.

Growth and Innovation

Lead the department that advances growth, innovation and sustainable revenue, strengthening existing business lines and developing new profitable ones through new markets, partnerships, customer segments, products, services and pricing.
Ensure opportunities are supported by market, financial, operational, governance, legal, tax and risk analysis, and turned into business cases and plans for the Executive Leadership Team and Boards that fit strategy, capacity and mandate.
Lead the adoption of artificial intelligence across the organization with sound governance, privacy, security, risk and change management and training, and watch for emerging technologies and business models that create member value.

Marketing and Communications

Provide strategic direction for marketing, brand, communications and major events, aligned with strategy, advocacy priorities, business objectives and member needs, with resources focused on the greatest value and a clear view of the return on major marketing spend.
Oversee major campaigns and events, including advertising, the annual Convention, advocacy and election campaigns, member engagement and brand initiatives, and guide internal communications so employees receive clear, timely and consistent information.
Translate complex organizational, policy and business issues into clear messages for members, elected officials, partners and other audiences.
Direct sensitive communications issues and media relations, shaping positioning and messaging with other executives to protect the organization’s reputation in a dynamic political environment.
Oversee marketing and brand strategy to strengthen awareness of Alberta Municipalities and its services and support the growth and positioning of its business lines.

Executive and People Leadership

Contribute to the leadership, direction and performance of the organization as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, and act on behalf of the Chief Executive Officer when assigned.
Coach the Senior Directors, set clear expectations and performance measures, and hold leaders accountable for results.
Build a collaborative, accountable and high performing culture that values member focus, strategic thinking, innovation and continuous improvement, and support strong relationships across departments, entities, Boards and committees.

QUALIFICATIONS

Significant experience leading enterprise strategic and corporate planning and delivering major cross functional programs and projects involving multiple departments, stakeholders and competing priorities.

Strong financial and business acumen, including assessing business cases, budgets, contracts, revenue opportunities, costs and risks.
Knowledge of governance practices, change management and innovation, with a strong understanding of economic, social, environmental, technological and political trends and their impact on members.
A degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Political Science, Strategic Management, Organizational Leadership or a related field.

Experience in a government, municipal, association, regulatory, political or other multi stakeholder environment.
Executive oversight of corporate planning and governance, growth and innovation, a project management office, or marketing, communications, engagement, brand strategy and major events.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Sets long-term strategy with other leaders, owns strategic goals and plans, presents strong business cases for initiatives and resource allocation, and anticipates obstacles and business disruptions.
Analyzes ambiguous information, applies frameworks where there is little precedent, seeks diverse views and makes sound decisions with organization wide consequences.

The Ontario Historical Society is seeking a new Executive Director, a unique and exciting opportunity to work with the diverse peoples of Ontario and make a significant contribution to the heritage sector in Canada.

What is the Ontario Historical Society?

Founded in 1888, The Ontario Historical Society (OHS) is a not-for-profit corporation and registered charity; a non-government group bringing together people of all ages, all walks of life and all cultural backgrounds interested in preserving some aspect of Ontario’s history.

The OHS is unique in its provincial mandate and very different to other provincial organizations. In 1899, the Legislative Assembly of Ontario granted OHS the legal power and responsibility to incorporate not-for-profit historical organizations. The Society is the only not-for-profit in North America with this legal tool to establish and incorporate other not-for-profit historical corporations.

The OHS is an inclusive, extensive membership-based organization, dedicated to working with all cultures, all religions and with Indigenous peoples. It is the largest organization of its kind in Canada that is growing through grassroots community engagement focused on the protection and promotion of Ontario’s history. 

The OHS headquarters is located at the historic John McKenzie House (built 1913) in Willowdale (Toronto), Ontario. John McKenzie House and its adjacent stable s and milk-house are all designated under the Ontario Heritage Act (1993). All buildings and adjacent properties (including Parkview Neighbourhood Garden) are subject to a heritage conservation easement (2013).

The OHS is governed by an all-volunteer board of directors. The Society is supported by and supports over 800+ member organizations and institutions located in communities across Ontario.

What does the OHS do?

●        Provides advice on all matters relating to good governance for historical not-for-profit corporations, including reviewing and revising constitutions and by-laws, surrendering charters, facilitating corporate name changes, consulting on the dissolution of assets, and supporting member applications for federal charitable tax status;
●        Oversees an insurance program at reduced cost to members in good standing;
●        Maintains corporate archives of all affiliated societies, which number over 335 not-for-profit organizations and growing;
●       Publishes in print and online the widely read peer-reviewed scholarly journal Ontario History (established 1899);
●        Provides consultations and other services to its affiliated societies and member organizations which includes, but is not limited to examining strategic directions, providing references for grant applications, consulting on heritage designations and conservation easements, and providing webinars and workshops on topics of heritage matters to both members and the broader heritage community;
●       Runs an awards program to honour individuals and organizations who have contributed significantly to the preservation and promotion of Ontario’s heritage;
●        Acts as an advocate in partnership with our member organizations, supporting the preservation and designation of heritage assets in local communities across the province;
●        Is the guardian of the public interest in regard to cemetery preservation in the province as it relates to The Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act, 2002 (FBCSA), formerly Cemeteries Act (Revised 1990). Compiles a detailed list of all unregistered cemeteries in Ontario as requested by the Government of Ontario; and
●        Maintains a reference library of over 5,600 books reflecting Ontario’s historical and cultural diversity.

Position Description:

The Executive Director reports to the Society’s board of directors and is charged with management roles, strategic leadership, and public advocacy that are needed to fulfill the unique mission and vision of the Society. In working to preserve, protect, and promote Ontario’s history and heritage, the Executive Director collaborates with the board of directors, with the Society membership, and with the affiliated societies, staff, and sector partners. The Executive Director is an effective leader, a trusted advisor and resource person, and a mentor to historical organizations throughout the province. The standard working hours for this position are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday in office. Flexibility is required to accommodate evening and weekend commitments, as necessary. In order to fulfill and advance the Society’s mission, willingness to travel throughout Ontario is part of the role.

Role and Responsibilities:

●        Oversees the unique legal responsibilities of the Society and represents the interests of historical organizations throughout the province.
●       R esponsible for the overall administration and financial management of the Society.
●       Cultivates productive working relationships with all levels of government and embraces public visibility and advocacy roles and responsibilities.
●       Serves as the Society spokesperson to address the public, policy makers, partners, and the media.
●       Collaborates with members and stakeholders to enhance public support and financial resources for OHS and its affiliates.
●       Leads and facilitates philanthropic activities, donor relations, and funding opportunities.
●       Oversees the maintenance and operation of the historic John McKenzie House property.
●       Guides, supervises, and evaluates organizational operations and personnel, delegating authority as is deemed appropriate to other staff.
●       Mentors staff and volunteers, maintaining a positive, productive, and collaborative working environment.
●       Oversees strategic planning and evaluation (including the effectiveness of programs, services and communications), and central office operations.
●       The Society’s new strategic plan is focused on expanding capacity building programs, supports, resources, and events for its members. The Executive Director will lead the organization in building new partnerships and strengthening existing operations to advance this strategic direction. 
●       Ensures adherence to policies, procedures, and performance standards; ensuring the Society is fully compliant, accountable, and transparent in regard to federal, provincial, and municipal laws and regulations.

●       Supports the work of the Editor and Book Editor of the Society’s scholarly journal Ontario History

Required Qualifications:

Qualified applicants must have a bachelor’s degree, with a master’s degree strongly preferred, and a minimum of eight ( 8
) years of leadership experience in the not-for-profit sector. Experience in public policy development and a successful advocacy track record at the federal, provincial, or municipal level is required. A broad knowledge of the public benefits and roles that government and philanthropic support play in advancing positive impacts provincially is fundamental. A comprehensive understanding and sensitivity of the mandates, values, and environments in which the Society, its affiliates and members function.

annually. Placement within the range will be based on demonstrated skills, and relevant experience.

no later than 11:59 pm EST on Wednesday, December 23, 2026. Interviews will be scheduled for the second week of January. We thank everyone for their interest, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted. References will be requested at the time of the interview.

The Ontario Historical Society is seeking a new Executive Director, a unique and exciting opportunity to work with the diverse peoples of Ontario and make a significant contribution to the heritage sector in Canada.

What is the Ontario Historical Society?

Founded in 1888, The Ontario Historical Society (OHS) is a not-for-profit corporation and registered charity; a non-government group bringing together people of all ages, all walks of life and all cultural backgrounds interested in preserving some aspect of Ontario’s history.

The OHS is unique in its provincial mandate and very different to other provincial organizations. In 1899, the Legislative Assembly of Ontario granted OHS the legal power and responsibility to incorporate not-for-profit historical organizations. The Society is the only not-for-profit in North America with this legal tool to establish and incorporate other not-for-profit historical corporations.

The OHS is an inclusive, extensive membership-based organization, dedicated to working with all cultures, all religions and with Indigenous peoples. It is the largest organization of its kind in Canada that is growing through grassroots community engagement focused on the protection and promotion of Ontario’s history. 

The OHS headquarters is located at the historic John McKenzie House (built 1913) in Willowdale (Toronto), Ontario. John McKenzie House and its adjacent stable s and milk-house are all designated under the Ontario Heritage Act (1993). All buildings and adjacent properties (including Parkview Neighbourhood Garden) are subject to a heritage conservation easement (2013).

The OHS is governed by an all-volunteer board of directors. The Society is supported by and supports over 800+ member organizations and institutions located in communities across Ontario.

What does the OHS do?

●        Provides advice on all matters relating to good governance for historical not-for-profit corporations, including reviewing and revising constitutions and by-laws, surrendering charters, facilitating corporate name changes, consulting on the dissolution of assets, and supporting member applications for federal charitable tax status;
●        Oversees an insurance program at reduced cost to members in good standing;
●        Maintains corporate archives of all affiliated societies, which number over 335 not-for-profit organizations and growing;
●       Publishes in print and online the widely read peer-reviewed scholarly journal Ontario History (established 1899);
●        Provides consultations and other services to its affiliated societies and member organizations which includes, but is not limited to examining strategic directions, providing references for grant applications, consulting on heritage designations and conservation easements, and providing webinars and workshops on topics of heritage matters to both members and the broader heritage community;
●       Runs an awards program to honour individuals and organizations who have contributed significantly to the preservation and promotion of Ontario’s heritage;
●        Acts as an advocate in partnership with our member organizations, supporting the preservation and designation of heritage assets in local communities across the province;
●        Is the guardian of the public interest in regard to cemetery preservation in the province as it relates to The Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act, 2002 (FBCSA), formerly Cemeteries Act (Revised 1990). Compiles a detailed list of all unregistered cemeteries in Ontario as requested by the Government of Ontario; and
●        Maintains a reference library of over 5,600 books reflecting Ontario’s historical and cultural diversity.

Position Description:

The Executive Director reports to the Society’s board of directors and is charged with management roles, strategic leadership, and public advocacy that are needed to fulfill the unique mission and vision of the Society. In working to preserve, protect, and promote Ontario’s history and heritage, the Executive Director collaborates with the board of directors, with the Society membership, and with the affiliated societies, staff, and sector partners. The Executive Director is an effective leader, a trusted advisor and resource person, and a mentor to historical organizations throughout the province. The standard working hours for this position are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday in office. Flexibility is required to accommodate evening and weekend commitments, as necessary. In order to fulfill and advance the Society’s mission, willingness to travel throughout Ontario is part of the role.

Role and Responsibilities:

●       R esponsible for the overall administration and financial management of the Society.

●       Serves as the Society spokesperson to address the public, policy makers, partners, and the media.
●       Collaborates with members and stakeholders to enhance public support and financial resources for OHS and its affiliates.
●       Leads and facilitates philanthropic activities, donor relations, and funding opportunities.
●       Oversees the maintenance and operation of the historic John McKenzie House property.
●       Guides, supervises, and evaluates organizational operations and personnel, delegating authority as is deemed appropriate to other staff.
●       Mentors staff and volunteers, maintaining a positive, productive, and collaborative working environment.
●       Oversees strategic planning and evaluation (including the effectiveness of programs, services and communications), and central office operations.
●       The Society’s new strategic plan is focused on expanding capacity building programs, supports, resources, and events for its members. The Executive Director will lead the organization in building new partnerships and strengthening existing operations to advance this strategic direction. 
●       Ensures adherence to policies, procedures, and performance standards; ensuring the Society is fully compliant, accountable, and transparent in regard to federal, provincial, and municipal laws and regulations.

●       Supports the work of the Editor and Book Editor of the Society’s scholarly journal Ontario History
